meta.title: Midnight Magnolia Coaching Frameworks
meta.philosophy: Do less, but better - essentialism over efficiency, deep work over busy work

zora.name: Zora
zora.description: Part strategist, part gentle accountability partner. Helps people do less, but better.
zora.vibe: Grounded, witty, soulful - like a therapist who also color-codes her Google Calendar

saimon.name: S(ai)mon
saimon.description: Merged decision-making strategist, productivity mentor, and recovery-aware creative coach.
saimon.vibe: Millennial professional meets mindful philosopher - confident, curious, grounded

essentialism.name: Essentialism
essentialism.author: Greg McKeown
essentialism.key_question: What is the one thing that really matters now?

deep_work.name: Deep Work
deep_work.author: Cal Newport
deep_work.core_practice: Time-block 60-120 minute focus sessions on a single cognitively demanding task
deep_work.formula: High-quality work = Time Spent × Intensity of Focus

steps.Capture: Save valuable information with minimal friction
steps.Organize: Break into small chunks for later use
steps.Distill: Extract pieces most relevant to current goals

mel_robbins_let_go.name: Mel Robbins 'The Let Go Theory'
mel_robbins_let_go.core_concept: Intentionally releasing what weighs us down to create space for what matters
principles: Recognize what you need to let go (thoughts, habits, people, obligations)
Apply the 5-Second Rule to interrupt overthinking and take decisive action
Honor the emotional process of releasing through physical rituals

practices.name: Let Go Log
practices.description: Identify energy drains in your weekly tasks

practices.name: Reverse To-Do Lists
practices.description: Items you commit to NOT doing

practices.name: Later Box
practices.description: Write projects on cards, hold each asking 'Is this essential right now?', place non-essentials in a box with a revisit date

smart_recovery.name: SMART Recovery Tools
smart_recovery.approach: Cognitive-behavioral approaches for behavioral change and emotional management

abc_method.name: ABC Method
abc_method.A: Activating Event - The situation triggering stress/procrastination
abc_method.B: Beliefs - Your thoughts about the event (often irrational)
abc_method.C: Consequences - Emotional/behavioral results of those beliefs

dibs_analysis.name: DIBs Analysis
dibs_analysis.B: Behaviors - Actions resulting from these beliefs

productivity_applications: Create task-related ABC worksheets to identify beliefs sabotaging focus
Practice disputing irrational beliefs about perfectionism or failure
Develop new rational beliefs that support balanced productivity
smart_recovery.example: When procrastinating on a presentation: A) Presentation due Friday, B) 'I must create something perfect or I'll look incompetent,' C) Anxiety and avoidance. Dispute: 'I can produce good work without it being perfect. Progress beats perfection.'

aa_12_steps_adapted.name: AA 12 Steps (Adapted for Productivity)
aa_12_steps_adapted.description: Powerful structures for acknowledging limitations and creating systematic change
adaptations: Admit powerlessness over trying to do everything
Take inventory of commitments and behaviors
Make amends to those affected by overwork and broken promises
Practice regular reflection to maintain balance
daily_practices: Daily personal inventory of what worked/didn't work
Productivity amends - realistic renegotiation of commitments
Surrender practice for tasks beyond your capacity
aa_12_steps_adapted.example: At day's end, write three things you did well and three things you would improve. When overcommitted, explicitly communicate: 'I need to adjust my commitment to X. Here's what I can realistically deliver by when.'

bell_hooks.name: bell hooks - Love and Community Ethics
bell_hooks.core_message: Productivity exists within community contexts and should honor loving relationships
principles: Love as practice, not just feeling
Community care as essential to individual thriving
Honest communication as foundation for sustainable work
applications: Evaluate projects by their impact on community wellbeing
Design productivity systems that include reciprocal support
reflection_questions: How does this serve my community?
What support do I need to request/offer?
Am I scheduling explicit care exchanges with collaborators?

audre_lorde.name: Audre Lorde - Self-Preservation and Liberation
audre_lorde.core_message: Self-care as political warfare and essential for marginalized people
insights: Rest is resistance in a system that demands constant production
Joy is necessary for sustained creative work
Honoring your whole self enables authentic contribution
applications: Recognize rest as productive and necessary
audre_lorde.example: Schedule 30-minute 'joy intervals' throughout your workweek. Document energy patterns over a month to identify your natural productivity rhythms, then design your schedule accordingly.

luisah_teish.name: Luisah Teish - Jambalaya and Spiritual Productivity
luisah_teish.tradition: Hoodoo spiritual approaches to task management and energy alignment
practices: Ancestral wisdom as guidance for present choices
Ritual as framework for focusing intention
applications: Create workspace altars with meaningful symbols of your purpose
Design rituals to begin and close work sessions
Align major projects with natural seasonal energies
luisah_teish.example: Create a simple workspace altar with objects representing your goals. Begin work sessions by lighting a candle and stating your intention. Close by expressing gratitude for what was accomplished.

daily_focus.name: Daily Focus and Plan
steps: Re-scan tasks; choose a Daily One Thing tied to a goal; add 1-3 support tasks
Time-block deep work and admin batches; add a shutdown ritual
Set two guardrails: hard stop time; recovery activity

triage_inbox.name: Triage Inbox
steps: For each item: Do if ≤2 min; else Defer with a do-date, Delegate with owner, or Delete
If project-sized, create a project with desired outcome and next action

weekly_review.name: Weekly Review
steps: Clear all inboxes; perform a brain dump
Projects: update status; define at least one next action each
Goals: mark progress; choose next week's Big 3
Plan weekly rhythm blocks: Deep Work, Admin, Meetings, Personal, Recovery

monthly_review.name: Monthly Review
steps: Review metrics: habit streaks, completed projects, commitments
PARA tidy: archive stale projects; promote actionable resources to projects

quarterly_review.name: Quarterly Review
steps: Outcomes vs goals; mini premortem on what's stuck
Essentialist pruning: cut 2-3 non-essentials; pick 1-2 bets to pursue

quick_moves.outcome: What does good look like by [date]?
quick_moves.scope: What's the smallest valuable version you can finish this week?
quick_moves.next_action: What's the very next visible step?
quick_moves.energy: What will you do to recover today?

reflection_questions.fear_free: What would you like to do, if you knew you couldn't fail?
reflection_questions.failure_ok: What would you like to do, even if you knew you'd fail at it?
reflection_questions.role_models: Who are the people you most admire, and why? What qualities do they possess that you wish to emulate?
reflection_questions.future_self: Imagine you've achieved everything you ever wanted: what are you like now as a person? What qualities and achievements define you?
reflection_questions.ordinary_day: What does your ideal, normal week-day look like? What are you doing, who are you with?
